sentences.text: Rule one also tells you what can sit alongside these rules, and there are four things to know.
First, local authorities can make special rules for a particular harbor, river or lake.
But those rules must conform as closely as possible to the Navigation Rules.
They can add to them, not throw them out.
Second, governments can allow extra lights and shapes for warships, convoys, and fishing fleets working together, and extra whistle signals for warships and convoys.
So if you see an odd light on a Navy ship, that’s why.
Third, traffic separation schemes, the highway lanes for big ships, are adopted internationally.
We’ll cover them in lesson four.
And fourth, a vessel of unusual construction that can’t place her lights exactly as required may use the closest alternative her government approves.
Inland, that’s called a certificate of alternative compliance.
